description:
kith-events/src/lib.rs lines 27-33: make_channel(capacity: usize) panics if capacity == 0. The doc comment documents this, but usize admits zero at the type level and there is no way for a caller to statically guarantee capacity > 0 without reading the doc.

The doc comment suggests: 'if you need a variable capacity, use std::num::NonZeroUsize at the call site to enforce the constraint before calling this function' — but the function signature itself does not accept NonZeroUsize, making this advice aspirational rather than enforced.

Since all production call sites use hardcoded non-zero literals this is low risk in practice, but the API surface is inconsistent: it documents a type that should be used but does not accept it.

Fix: change the signature to make_channel(capacity: std::num::NonZeroUsize). This eliminates the panic entirely and makes the contract visible to the compiler. Or at minimum, accept NonZeroUsize to force callers with variable capacity to validate before calling.
title: kith-events: make_channel panic precondition not enforceable at call site
